question: Your support agent, built with the Claude Agent SDK, calls the lookup_order MCP tool to check whether an order is eligible for a return. When the order database times out, lookup_order returns the timeout message as a normal successful result. The agent then tells customers that their order does not exist. How should lookup_order communicate this failure back to the agent?

options.text: Add a system prompt instruction that tells the agent to scan every lookup_order result for words such as timeout or failed before trusting it.
options.reason: The guide does not rely on text matching for this; it says the tool should signal the failure with the isError flag, and the result would still be marked as successful.

options.text: Make lookup_order retry the database call in a loop until it succeeds, so that the agent never receives any failure result from the tool.
options.reason: The guide says tool failures should be communicated back to the agent through the isError flag; an endless hidden retry gives the agent no failure signal and no basis for a recovery decision.

options.text: Make lookup_order call escalate_to_human directly on every failure, without returning anything to the agent about what happened to the lookup.
options.reason: The guide says failures should be communicated back to the agent with the isError flag; hiding them stops the agent from choosing its own recovery and works against first-contact resolution.

options.text: Return the timeout details in the tool result with the isError flag set to true, so the agent knows the lookup failed.
options.reason: The guide names the MCP isError flag as the pattern for communicating tool failures back to the agent, so the agent can tell a failure apart from real order data.
